window_notes: Treat only if ALSO <10 inflorescences per shoot AND <20% fertile flowers (poor bloom); otherwise tolerate. RAIF Malaga 2025: 10.1% attacked, 6.2 infl/shoot, 27% fertile flowers.

window_notes: Highest dose on first application, lower on later ones; schedule Jun-Sep. Surround WP: max 1 application; Argical Pro: max 6, PHI 28 d. Also cited as heat-stress protection by Junta. No source for application to open flowers.

window_notes: RPI: intervene when 20% fruits with viable eggs AND 20% of eggs hatched (hatched 56% in Malaga Jun 2025). Eggs not viable at RH <30% (MAPA).
action: Intervene per RPI; preserve Chrysoperla (cut egg viability up to 50%)

window_notes: NAV threshold: no official action threshold found in fetched sources (EcuRed wiki 1 female per 10 shoots rejected as low-authority). Population peak July when mobile nymphs emerge (Valencia 2003-05).
action: Monitor; if above threshold treat late Jul-early Aug when all eggs hatched

window_notes: Deficit-irrigated table-olive trees irrigated only if midday SWP below -2.0 MPa; no yield reduction (Manzanilla, Sevilla, 3 seasons). Pit hardening began ~10-17 Jun there. Control target -1.4 MPa after massive pit hardening.
action: Irrigate by shortfall relative to threshold: <15% below -> 25% of max ETc (1 mm/d); 15-30% -> 50% (2 mm/d); >30% -> 100% (4 mm/d). Max ETc of orchard 4 mm/d.

window_notes: Irrigated-control target after massive pit hardening (-1.2 MPa before).
action: Full irrigation scheduling target

window_notes: Table olive Manzanilla: -2 MPa RDI vs -3.5 MPa severe RDI; yield not significantly affected but fruit drop and size related to stress; RDI feasible up to 12 t/ha without losing fruit size. Corell 2020 warns oil-olive thresholds may not transfer to table olives.
action: Avoid severe stress for table olive; use milder deficit

window_notes: FAO-56 Table 12 olives (40-60% ground cover): Kc ini 0.65, mid 0.70, end 0.70. Generic, not pit-hardening-specific; column order matched by position in fetched text. Use to convert ETo to ETc before applying % ETc rules.
